description.short_caption: Graph of SARS cases by date of hospitalization in Singapore, February 25 to March 22, 2003.
description.detailed_description: This is a bar graph displaying the number of SARS cases in Singapore by date of hospitalization between February 25 and March 22, 2003. The x-axis represents the date of onset, while the y-axis shows the number of cases. The bars are color-coded to represent different transmission categories: index (blue), primary (yellow), secondary (pink), and tertiary (red). A notable annotation highlights a case-patient transit event on March 17. The graph provides a visual representation of the outbreak's progression and transmission dynamics.
visible_findings: Bar graph with dates on the x-axis and case counts on the y-axis.
Color-coded bars indicating transmission categories: index, primary, secondary, tertiary.
Annotation marking a case-patient transit event on March 17.

One red blood cell contains a schizont, a stage of a Plasmodium parasite, characterized by multiple small nuclei or merozoites within the cell. The staining highlights the parasite's internal structures, aiding in its identification.

one red blood cell containing a schizont
multiple nuclei or merozoites visible within the schizont

description.short_caption: Histopathology of intestinal biopsy showing crypt architecture and inflammatory infiltrate.

The architecture of the crypts is visible, with a dense inflammatory infiltrate in the lamina propria. The infiltrate appears to consist of numerous lymphocytes and plasma cells. The epithelial lining of the crypts is intact, and there is no evidence of ulceration or necrosis in this section.
visible_findings: dense inflammatory infiltrate in lamina propria

description.short_caption: Immunoperoxidase stain highlighting organisms in gastrointestinal biopsy.

The background tissue is counterstained in a light blue color, providing contrast to the immunoperoxidase-positive areas.
visible_findings: light blue counterstain highlighting tissue architecture
crypts and villi of gastrointestinal mucosa visible

description.detailed_description: This lateral radiograph of the lumbar spine demonstrates irregularities in the vertebral bodies, including loss of disc space and possible bony destruction. The image suggests potential infectious or degenerative processes affecting the lumbar vertebrae. The alignment appears disrupted, and there may be evidence of sclerosis or lytic changes. The findings are consistent with conditions such as osteomyelitis or discitis.

description.short_caption: Axial abdominal CT scan showing bowel loops and intra-abdominal structures.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT scan of the abdomen shows multiple loops of bowel, some of which appear distended with gas and fluid. The vertebral body is visible in the center, and surrounding soft tissues and intra-abdominal structures are present. There is a large, rounded, hypodense area in the left side of the image, suggestive of a fluid-filled or cystic structure. The scan is without contrast, as no enhancement is visible.
visible_findings: hypodense rounded structure in the left abdomen

description.short_caption: Axial T2-weighted MRI showing brain abnormalities at 12 months.
description.detailed_description: This axial T2-weighted MRI image of the brain shows prominent abnormalities, including hyperintense lesions in the periventricular white matter and basal ganglia. There is evidence of ventricular enlargement and cortical atrophy, suggesting chronic or progressive pathology. The image demonstrates clear contrast between the lesions and surrounding tissue, aiding in the visualization of structural changes.
visible_findings: hyperintense lesions in periventricular white matter

description.short_caption: GMS stain of transbronchial biopsy showing fungal elements (100x magnification).
description.detailed_description: This image shows a transbronchial biopsy stained with Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) at 100x magnification. The background consists of lung tissue with pale green staining, typical of GMS. Dark, round to oval fungal elements are visible, consistent with yeast forms. These fungal structures are highlighted in black against the green-stained tissue, aiding in identification.
visible_findings: lung tissue stained green with GMS
dark oval fungal elements consistent with yeast forms
contrast between fungal structures and tissue background

description.short_caption: Acid-fast bacillus highlighted in a stained preparation.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a microscopic field stained with a technique highlighting acid-fast organisms, likely Ziehl-Neelsen or Kinyoun stain. A single, slender, pink rod-shaped structure is visible against a blue background, consistent with an acid-fast bacillus. The surrounding blue material appears to be cellular debris or tissue. The contrast between the pink bacillus and the blue background is characteristic of this staining method.
visible_findings: blue background suggestive of cellular material or debris

description.short_caption: GMS stain of transbronchial biopsy showing fungal elements (100x magnification).
description.detailed_description: This image shows a transbronchial biopsy stained with Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) at 100x magnification. The tissue exhibits fungal elements, including a prominent round structure consistent with a fungal spore. The background consists of lung parenchyma with light green staining, typical of GMS highlighting fungal cell walls. The dark staining of the fungal elements contrasts sharply with the surrounding tissue.
visible_findings: contrast between fungal elements and surrounding tissue

description.short_caption: Microscopic view of fungal elements with hyphae and budding yeast forms.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a microscopic view of fungal elements, including branching hyphae and numerous budding yeast forms. The organisms are stained to enhance visibility, with the hyphae appearing as elongated structures and the yeast forms as round or oval buds. The image is taken under high magnification, likely using a light microscope.

description.short_caption: Axial contrast-enhanced CT of the pelvis showing a central pelvic mass.
description.detailed_description: This axial contrast-enhanced CT image of the pelvis demonstrates a centrally located mass with a heterogeneous appearance. The mass appears to be within the pelvic cavity, possibly involving or adjacent to pelvic organs. Surrounding soft tissues and bony structures are visible, and the contrast enhancement highlights the vascular structures and tissue planes. The image is de-identified and suitable for educational purposes.
visible_findings: visible pelvic bones and soft tissues

description.short_caption: Diffuse maculopapular rash on the back.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the back of an individual with a diffuse maculopapular rash. The rash consists of small, erythematous macules and papules distributed across the skin. The image is well-lit, and the rash appears to be non-vesicular and non-confluent. The patient is wearing a patterned top, and no other abnormalities are visible in the surrounding skin.

description.short_caption: Linear erythematous lesions on the forearm, two months after treatment.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the forearm of a patient with linear erythematous lesions extending proximally from the wrist. The lesions appear to follow a lymphatic distribution, with some areas of mild scabbing or crusting, particularly near the wrist. The surrounding skin is otherwise unremarkable, and there is no visible swelling or significant discoloration beyond the lesions.
visible_findings: scabbing or crusting near the wrist

description.short_caption: Axial contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showing dilated bowel loops with air-fluid levels.
description.detailed_description: This axial contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen demonstrates multiple dilated bowel loops with air-fluid levels, suggestive of bowel obstruction. The contrast highlights the bowel lumen and surrounding structures. There is no clear evidence of free intraperitoneal air, but the findings are consistent with a mechanical obstruction or ileus. The scan is preoperative, as indicated in the case caption.

Case_03023/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin stain of transbronchial biopsy (20x).

description.short_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin stain of transbronchial biopsy showing lung parenchyma with inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows lung parenchyma stained with hematoxylin and eosin at 20x magnification. The tissue demonstrates areas of inflammation with cellular infiltrates, including lymphocytes and possibly other inflammatory cells, within the interstitial spaces. There are also alveolar spaces visible, some of which appear collapsed or partially filled. The overall architecture suggests an inflammatory process, potentially consistent with an infectious or interstitial lung condition.
visible_findings: inflammatory cellular infiltrates in interstitial spaces
alveolar spaces, some collapsed or partially filled

description.short_caption: Bacterial colonies on a culture plate from a wound specimen.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a round culture plate with bacterial colonies growing on an agar medium. The colonies appear as small, raised, and pigmented formations, with some showing a brownish coloration. The plate is labeled with 'PVD,' and there are black redactions obscuring parts of the image. The background is a textured surface, likely a laboratory bench. The colonies suggest microbial growth from a wound specimen.
visible_findings: black redactions obscuring parts of the image

description.short_caption: Ulcerated lesion with erythematous border and central necrotic tissue.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows an ulcerated lesion on the skin of an extremity. The lesion has a central area of necrotic tissue with a yellowish appearance, surrounded by erythema and mild swelling. The edges of the lesion are irregular, and there is no visible purulent drainage. The surrounding skin appears inflamed.

Case_03025/figure3.jpg.source_caption: H and E stain of peritoneal serosa biopsy.

description.short_caption: H and E stain of peritoneal serosa biopsy showing granulomatous inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of peritoneal serosa stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H and E). The tissue demonstrates granulomatous inflammation characterized by a central area of necrosis surrounded by epithelioid macrophages and multinucleated giant cells. The background contains scattered lymphocytes and fibroblasts. The findings are consistent with a granulomatous process, potentially infectious or inflammatory in origin.

description.short_caption: Axial abdominal CT scan showing intra-abdominal findings.
description.detailed_description: This is an axial view of an abdominal CT scan without clear evidence of contrast enhancement. The image shows the abdominal cavity with visible loops of bowel, vertebral column, and surrounding soft tissues. There appears to be some gas-filled bowel loops and possible soft tissue densities, but no obvious large masses or fluid collections are immediately apparent. The scan is oriented with the right side of the patient on the left of the image (R) and the left side on the right (L).
visible_findings: axial CT view of the abdomen
soft tissue structures surrounding the bowel

description.short_caption: Pelvic MRI scan showing coronal view of the pelvis.
description.detailed_description: This is a coronal MRI image of the pelvis. The bony structures, including the pelvis and sacrum, are clearly visible. Soft tissue structures within the pelvic cavity are also discernible, though no obvious abnormalities are apparent in this image. The image appears to be a T1-weighted sequence based on the contrast between fat and other tissues.
visible_findings: bony structures of the pelvis and sacrum
soft tissue structures within the pelvic cavity

description.short_caption: Calcofluor stain of spun urine showing fungal elements (400x).
description.detailed_description: This image shows a fluorescent microscopy view of a calcofluor white stain preparation of spun urine sediment at 400x magnification. The fungal element appears as a bright green, rounded structure with internal detail, consistent with yeast morphology. The calcofluor stain binds to chitin and cellulose in fungal cell walls, causing them to fluoresce under UV light.
visible_findings: internal detail consistent with yeast morphology

Case_03025/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Calcofluor stain of spun peritoneal fluid (400x).

description.short_caption: Calcofluor stain of spun peritoneal fluid showing fungal elements (400x).
description.detailed_description: This image shows a fluorescent green-stained structure under a Calcofluor white stain viewed at 400x magnification. The structure appears rounded with irregular edges and internal granularity, consistent with fungal elements. Calcofluor binds to chitin and cellulose in fungal cell walls, causing fluorescence under UV light. The background is dark, enhancing the visibility of the fluorescent structure.

description.short_caption: Axial pelvic MRI showing bilateral pelvic masses.
description.detailed_description: This axial pelvic MRI image reveals bilateral pelvic masses that are hyperintense relative to surrounding tissues. The masses are located adjacent to the pelvic organs, with clear demarcation from the surrounding structures. The image is de-identified and shows no personal identifiers. The scan provides a detailed view of the pelvic anatomy, including the bony pelvis and soft tissues.
visible_findings: clear demarcation of masses from surrounding tissues
visualization of pelvic bones and soft tissues

description.short_caption: Lactophenol cotton blue stain of joint aspirate showing fungal hyphae and spores.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a lactophenol cotton blue stain of a joint aspirate. The field contains branching, septate fungal hyphae and numerous round spores, consistent with a fungal organism. The stain highlights the fungal structures in blue against a pale background. This is indicative of a fungal infection in the joint, such as septic arthritis caused by a fungal pathogen.

description.short_caption: Erythematous, vesicular, and crusted lesions on the cheek.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows a close-up view of the cheek with erythematous patches, vesicles, and crusted lesions. The lesions are irregularly distributed and appear inflamed, with some areas showing superficial erosion. The surrounding skin appears mildly erythematous. The findings suggest an infectious or inflammatory process.

description.short_caption: Lactophenol cotton blue stain showing fungal hyphae and spores from joint aspiration.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a lactophenol cotton blue stain of joint fluid aspirate. The fungal elements are clearly visible, with septate hyphae and numerous round spores. The hyphae are branching, and the spores are distributed along the hyphal structures. The staining highlights the fungal morphology, aiding in the identification of fungal infection in the joint.

Case_03027/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Abdominal CT scan three days later.

description.short_caption: Abdominal CT scan showing a fluid collection with surrounding inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This axial abdominal CT scan demonstrates a well-defined fluid collection in the left retroperitoneal region, with surrounding fat stranding indicative of inflammation. Adjacent bowel loops appear displaced but not directly involved. The vertebral body and surrounding musculature are visible, with no obvious bony abnormalities. The scan is non-contrast, as no enhancement is visible.
visible_findings: fluid collection in the left retroperitoneal region

description.short_caption: Histological stain of the aorta showing bacterial organisms.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a histological section of the aorta stained to highlight bacterial organisms. Numerous small, rod-shaped bacteria are visible, distributed throughout the tissue. The background tissue appears disrupted, with areas of necrosis and inflammatory infiltrates. The staining technique enhances the contrast between the bacteria and the surrounding tissue, aiding in their identification.

description.short_caption: Histopathology of the aorta showing inflammatory infiltrates.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of the aorta stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The tissue demonstrates dense inflammatory infiltrates predominantly composed of mononuclear cells within the vessel wall. There is evidence of disruption of the normal architecture, with areas of fibrinoid necrosis and possible involvement of the media. The background shows eosinophilic staining of connective tissue and scattered nuclei.

description.short_caption: Histopathology of a cheek punch biopsy showing inflammatory infiltrate.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The image reveals a dense inflammatory infiltrate composed predominantly of lymphocytes, with scattered plasma cells and histiocytes. The surrounding tissue shows evidence of edema and mild architectural disruption. No clear granulomas or organisms are visible at this magnification.

Case_03028/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2: Hematoxylin and eosin stain of facial punch biopsy.

description.short_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin stain of a facial punch biopsy showing dermal inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This hematoxylin and eosin-stained section of a facial punch biopsy shows the epidermis and dermis. The epidermis appears intact, while the dermis exhibits dense inflammatory infiltrates, predominantly perivascular. There is no clear evidence of granulomas or necrosis in this image. Hair follicles and adnexal structures are visible, with no overt signs of destruction.
visible_findings: visible hair follicles and adnexal structures

description.short_caption: Clinical image of the left knee showing multiple skin lesions and scarring.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the left knee of a patient with multiple skin lesions. There are areas of scarring and ulceration, with one lesion marked by an arrow. The surrounding skin appears erythematous, and there is evidence of prior trauma or infection. The image suggests a localized infectious or inflammatory process.
visible_findings: multiple skin lesions on the left knee

description.short_caption: Giemsa stain of a punch biopsy showing inflammatory cells and possible intracellular organisms.
description.detailed_description: This Giemsa-stained image of a punch biopsy reveals numerous inflammatory cells, including lymphocytes and histiocytes, with some cells containing intracellular organisms. The background shows a mix of extracellular matrix and scattered cellular debris. The staining highlights nuclear and cytoplasmic details, with organisms appearing as small, dark-staining structures within some cells.
visible_findings: Giemsa stain highlighting nuclear and cytoplasmic details

description.short_caption: Radiograph of the knee showing joint abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This image shows an anteroposterior and lateral radiograph of the knee. There is evidence of joint space narrowing, particularly in the medial compartment, and possible subchondral sclerosis. The bony structures appear irregular, suggesting degenerative or infectious changes. No obvious fractures are visible. The soft tissue outlines are faint but appear unremarkable.

description.short_caption: Histopathology showing a cluster of organisms with surrounding inflammatory cells.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a dense cluster of organisms stained in bright magenta, surrounded by a background of inflammatory cells. The organisms appear to be aggregated, and the surrounding tissue exhibits cellular infiltrates consistent with an inflammatory response. The stain used highlights the organisms distinctly against the background, suggesting a special stain such as PAS or GMS.
visible_findings: contrast between organisms and background tissue

description.short_caption: CT scan of the knee showing joint effusion and possible bone involvement.
description.detailed_description: This image shows axial CT slices of the knee joint at multiple levels. There is evidence of joint effusion, visible as a hypodense area surrounding the joint space. The cortical bone appears irregular in some slices, suggesting possible bone involvement, such as osteomyelitis or erosion. The soft tissue surrounding the joint appears swollen, which may indicate inflammation or infection.
visible_findings: joint effusion visible as hypodense areas
irregular cortical bone in some slices
soft tissue swelling around the joint

description.short_caption: Histopathology of gastrointestinal biopsy showing a parasitic structure within the mucosa.
description.detailed_description: This histopathological image shows a section of gastrointestinal mucosa stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The mucosal architecture is visible, with crypts and epithelial lining. A prominent round parasitic structure is embedded within the mucosa, surrounded by inflammatory cells. The parasite appears to have a thick wall and internal structures, consistent with a helminth or protozoan cyst.
visible_findings: gastrointestinal mucosa with crypts and epithelial lining
round parasitic structure within the mucosa

Case_03030/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Skin findings on the eighth day.

description.detailed_description: The image shows a close-up view of the skin with a single erythematous papule that has a central ulceration. The lesion is surrounded by a slightly raised red border, and the central area appears to have a small depression or crust. The surrounding skin is otherwise unremarkable. The text overlay indicates this was observed on the eighth day.

description.short_caption: Erythematous papule on the skin observed on the sixth hospital day.

The surrounding skin appears unremarkable, with no significant swelling or additional lesions visible. The photograph is well-lit, allowing clear visualization of the lesion's characteristics.

Case_03030/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Cervical lymph node, H and E stain (x 400 magnification).

description.short_caption: Cervical lymph node, H&E stain at high magnification showing granulomatous inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of a cervical lymph node stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) at high magnification. The field reveals granulomatous inflammation characterized by clusters of epithelioid macrophages, multinucleated giant cells, and scattered lymphocytes. The background contains areas of necrosis and cellular debris, indicative of caseating granulomas. These findings are consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process, such as tuberculosis or fungal infection.

Case_03030/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Chest CT scan on the sixth day.

description.short_caption: Chest CT scan showing bilateral pulmonary findings.
description.detailed_description: This image shows axial CT slices of the chest at different levels. The lung windows (right panels) reveal bilateral ground-glass opacities and patchy consolidations, predominantly in the lower lobes. The mediastinal windows (left panels) show no significant lymphadenopathy or pleural effusion. These findings are consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process, potentially viral or bacterial pneumonia.

Case_03030/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Cervical lymph node PAS stain x 1000.

description.short_caption: Cervical lymph node PAS stain showing fungal elements at high magnification.
description.detailed_description: This is a histopathological image of a cervical lymph node stained with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) at high magnification (x1000). The image shows numerous round to oval fungal elements with thick walls and occasional budding forms, consistent with yeast-like organisms. The surrounding tissue exhibits a pink background with inflammatory cells and some necrosis. The PAS stain highlights the fungal cell walls in magenta, aiding in their identification.
visible_findings: PAS stain highlighting fungal cell walls in magenta

description.short_caption: Extensive ulcerations on the lower leg and foot with exposed dermis.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the lower leg and foot of a patient with multiple large, irregularly shaped ulcerations. The ulcers have well-demarcated borders and expose the underlying dermis, which appears red and moist. Surrounding skin is hyperpigmented, with some areas showing mild swelling. The foot is partially submerged in water, suggesting a possible wound care or soaking procedure. The ulcers are located on the anterior lower leg and dorsum of the foot.

description.short_caption: Radiograph of the left leg with external fixation.
description.detailed_description: This is a lateral radiograph of the left leg showing the distal femur and proximal tibia. An external fixation device is visible, with multiple screws and rods stabilizing the bone. The bone appears intact without obvious fractures or dislocations, but the fixation suggests prior trauma or surgical intervention. The soft tissues are not well visualized in this modality.
visible_findings: external fixation device with screws and rods
lateral view of distal femur and proximal tibia

description.short_caption: Erythematous maculopapular rash on the lower legs and feet.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the lower legs and feet of a patient with a diffuse erythematous maculopapular rash. The lesions are small, pink to red, and distributed across the dorsal aspects of the feet and lower legs. The rash appears non-confluent and is more prominent on the lateral aspects. The background skin tone is otherwise unremarkable. The image is well-lit and taken from a frontal perspective.
visible_findings: involvement of dorsal feet and lower legs

description.short_caption: Post-surgical follow-up of an external fixation device on the lower extremity.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a clinical photograph of a lower extremity with an external fixation device in place. A linear surgical scar is visible along the midline of the limb, suggesting prior surgical intervention. The surrounding skin appears intact without overt signs of infection, erythema, or drainage. The external fixation hardware is secured to the limb, with no visible complications such as hardware loosening or misalignment.

description.short_caption: Rash with erythematous macules and papules on the sole of the foot.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the sole of a foot with numerous small erythematous macules and papules distributed across the central and medial aspects. The lesions are discrete and non-confluent, with no visible vesicles, pustules, or ulceration. The surrounding skin appears otherwise normal. The image is well-lit and focuses on the plantar surface.

Case_03030/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Cervical lymph node, H and E stain (x 100 magnification).

description.short_caption: H&E stain of cervical lymph node at 100x magnification.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of a cervical lymph node stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) at 100x magnification. The tissue demonstrates areas of necrosis with pink eosinophilic debris and scattered basophilic nuclear remnants. Surrounding the necrotic areas, there are lymphoid cells and granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells. The architecture of the lymph node appears disrupted, consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process.

description.short_caption: Erythematous maculopapular rash on the dorsal aspect of the foot.
description.detailed_description: This image shows the dorsal aspect of a foot with a diffuse erythematous maculopapular rash. The lesions are small, discrete, and scattered across the skin surface. The background skin appears otherwise normal, with no visible signs of swelling or ulceration. The photograph is well-lit, and the rash is clearly visible against the lighter skin tone.

description.short_caption: Chest CT scan showing bilateral pulmonary findings.

The findings are distributed bilaterally and appear more prominent in the peripheral lung fields. The trachea and main bronchi are visible and appear patent. No significant pleural effusion or pneumothorax is noted.

description.short_caption: MRI scan of both feet showing soft tissue and bone structures.
description.detailed_description: This is an MRI scan of both feet, displayed in a coronal view. The image shows detailed visualization of soft tissues, bones, and joints. There appear to be areas of altered signal intensity in the soft tissues and possibly within the bones, which may suggest infection, inflammation, or other pathology. The scan is de-identified and includes a scale for reference.

areas of altered signal intensity in soft tissues

description.short_caption: Erythematous maculopapular rash on the plantar surface of the foot.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the plantar surface of a foot with numerous erythematous maculopapular lesions. The lesions are distributed diffusely across the sole, with some areas appearing more confluent. The skin surrounding the lesions appears otherwise intact, with no visible ulceration or scaling. description.short_caption: Axial CT scan of the neck showing soft tissue swelling.

The background tissue is counterstained in a lighter blue, highlighting the cellular architecture. No intravenous contrast is evident, as the bowel and vascular structures lack enhancement.

Case_07007/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Iodine stain of a stool specimen.

description.short_caption: Iodine stain of a stool specimen showing helminth ova and larvae.
description.detailed_description: This image shows an iodine-stained stool specimen under light microscopy. Multiple curved, elongated structures consistent with helminth larvae are visible, along with rounded structures resembling helminth ova. The background contains debris and other particulate matter. The staining highlights the internal structures of the organisms, aiding in their identification.

Case_07007/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Gram stain of a sputum specimen.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing spiral-shaped bacteria in a sputum specimen.
description.detailed_description: This Gram stain image shows spiral-shaped bacteria, consistent with spirochetes, against a background of scattered cellular debris and smaller bacterial forms. The spirochetes appear as elongated, coiled structures with a dark purple stain, indicative of their Gram-negative nature. The image suggests a respiratory specimen, likely sputum, as the source.

Case_07008/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Figure 1. Gram stain of blood culture.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing branching gram-positive bacilli from a blood culture.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a blood culture with prominent branching, filamentous structures stained pink, consistent with gram-positive bacilli. The background contains scattered debris and other cellular material. The branching morphology is characteristic of certain bacterial species, such as Nocardia or Actinomyces. The image is magnified to highlight the bacterial structures.

description.short_caption: Thin blood smear showing intraerythrocytic ring forms.
description.detailed_description: This is a thin blood smear stained with Giemsa, showing numerous red blood cells with a single cell containing intraerythrocytic ring forms. The ring forms are characterized by a central vacuole and a thin cytoplasmic ring, consistent with Plasmodium species, indicative of malaria. The background shows a clear field with evenly distributed red blood cells.
visible_findings: red blood cells with uniform morphology
reveal_triggers: ring forms in red blood cells

Case_07006/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Thin smear of whole blood specimen.

description.short_caption: Thin smear of whole blood showing intraerythrocytic ring forms.
description.detailed_description: This is a thin smear of whole blood stained with Giemsa stain. The image shows numerous red blood cells, most of which appear normal in size and shape. A single red blood cell contains an intraerythrocytic ring form, consistent with a parasitic infection such as malaria. The background is clear, and no significant leukocytes or platelets are visible in this field.
visible_findings: red blood cells with normal morphology

description.short_caption: Axial CT scan of the brain showing hypodense areas.

The image shows hypodense areas in the brain parenchyma, particularly in the left hemisphere, which may suggest ischemic changes or edema. The ventricles appear slightly compressed, and there is no obvious midline shift. The orbits and surrounding structures are visible at the top of the image.
visible_findings: hypodense areas in the brain parenchyma

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing branching, filamentous Gram-positive organisms.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a blood culture. It reveals branching, filamentous structures that stain Gram-positive (red in this stain preparation). These structures are consistent with filamentous bacteria, such as Nocardia or Actinomyces. The background contains scattered cellular debris and other non-specific material.

description.short_caption: Fungal colonies with characteristic morphology on culture plate.

The colonies are circular with a central dense area and a lighter, fuzzy periphery, consistent with fungal growth. The plate appears to have an orange background, and the colonies exhibit a whitish-gray coloration. The morphology suggests filamentous fungi, but the specific organism cannot be definitively identified from this image alone.

description.short_caption: Gram stain of spun CSF showing gram-negative diplococci.
description.detailed_description: This Gram stain image shows numerous gram-negative diplococci, which appear as paired, pink-staining, kidney-shaped bacteria. The background contains cellular debris and faintly stained material, consistent with a spun cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) sample. The morphology and staining pattern are characteristic of gram-negative organisms, possibly Neisseria species.

Case_07009/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Gram stain of CSF, with gram negative diplococci (arrows).

description.short_caption: Gram stain of CSF showing gram-negative diplococci (arrows).
description.detailed_description: This is a high-magnification image of a Gram stain preparation of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Numerous pink-staining (gram-negative) diplococci are visible, some of which are indicated by arrows. The organisms are surrounded by a background of cellular debris and other structures consistent with CSF. The morphology and staining characteristics are consistent with gram-negative diplococci, which may suggest Neisseria meningitidis in the appropriate clinical context.

Case_07010/figure4.jpg.source_caption: H and E stain of resected sigmoid colon.

description.short_caption: H&E stain of sigmoid colon showing inflammatory infiltrates and granuloma formation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of the sigmoid colon stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The tissue demonstrates prominent inflammatory infiltrates, including numerous lymphocytes and plasma cells, as well as a granuloma with a central multinucleated giant cell. The background includes fibrous tissue and scattered inflammatory cells, consistent with chronic inflammation. The findings suggest a granulomatous process, potentially related to an infectious or autoimmune etiology.
visible_findings: granuloma with central multinucleated giant cell

Case_07010/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Immunohistochemical staining of colon specimen for CMV.

description.short_caption: Immunohistochemical staining of colon tissue showing CMV inclusions.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a high-magnification view of colon tissue stained using immunohistochemistry. Large, dark brown inclusions are visible within some cells, consistent with cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection. The background tissue is counterstained in a lighter hue, highlighting the nuclei and cytoplasm of surrounding cells. The staining pattern is specific for CMV antigens, aiding in the identification of infected cells.

Case_07009/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Chocolate agar plate with N. meningitidis colonies.

description.short_caption: Chocolate agar plate with bacterial colonies.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a chocolate agar plate with numerous small, round, and smooth bacterial colonies. The colonies are distributed in streak patterns, indicating a streak plate technique for bacterial isolation. The chocolate agar medium appears brown and opaque, characteristic of its composition, which supports the growth of fastidious organisms such as Neisseria species. The colonies are consistent with the morphology of Neisseria meningitidis, but definitive identification would require further testing.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary findings.

The cardiac silhouette appears normal in size, and there is no obvious pleural effusion. The bony structures, including the ribs and spine, are intact. Medical devices, such as ECG leads, are visible on the skin surface.

Case_07010/figure5.jpg.source_caption: H and E stain of colon, showing giant cell (arrows).

description.short_caption: H&E stain of colon showing a giant cell (arrows).

The image highlights a multinucleated giant cell, marked by arrows, surrounded by a background of inflammatory cells, including lymphocytes and histiocytes. The tissue architecture shows evidence of inflammation, with cellular infiltration and possible disruption of normal structure. The pink eosinophilic cytoplasm and purple nuclear staining are characteristic of the H&E technique.
visible_findings: multinucleated giant cell marked by arrows
inflammatory cell infiltrate including lymphocytes and histiocytes
pink eosinophilic cytoplasm and purple nuclear staining
disrupted tissue architecture indicative of inflammation

description.short_caption: Bilateral eye involvement with yellow discharge and eyelid swelling.

yellow crusting near the medial canthus of the right eye

description.short_caption: Axial MRI of the head showing orbital and intracranial structures.

no visible mass lesions or midline shift

description.short_caption: Gram stain of CSF showing numerous neutrophils and gram-negative diplococci.

Among the neutrophils, there are gram-negative diplococci, appearing as paired, pink-staining cocci. The findings are consistent with a bacterial meningitis caused by a gram-negative organism, such as Neisseria meningitidis.

description.short_caption: Multiple erythematous macules and papules on the back.

Case_07010/figure3.jpg.source_caption: H and E stain of resected sigmoid colon.

description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of the sigmoid colon stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The mucosal layer displays crypt architecture, with goblet cells visible. The submucosa appears expanded with inflammatory infiltrates and possible edema. The muscularis propria is partially visible at the lower edge. The staining highlights cellular and structural details, aiding in the identification of pathological changes.

description.short_caption: Clinical photograph showing conjunctival injection and mild eyelid swelling.

description.short_caption: Erythematous macules and plaques on the back.

The surrounding skin appears unremarkable, and no vesicles or pustules are visible. The image is well-focused, highlighting the texture and distribution of the rash.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing left-sided opacity.

The lesions are symmetric and appear darker than the surrounding brain parenchyma, consistent with areas of edema or infarction. arrows pointing to key cystic structures

The scan appears to be performed without intravenous contrast, as there is no clear enhancement of vascular structures.

description.short_caption: Histopathology showing spirochetes in a tissue sample stained with Warthin-Starry silver stain.
description.detailed_description: This histopathological image demonstrates a tissue section stained with Warthin-Starry silver stain, highlighting spirochetes (indicated by arrows) as thin, dark, spiral-shaped organisms. The background shows a dense inflammatory infiltrate with numerous cells, likely representing a host immune response. The spirochetes are distributed in the tissue, consistent with an infectious etiology such as syphilis. The stain enhances the visibility of these organisms against the cellular background.

description.short_caption: Acid-fast bacilli (AFB) visible on stained smear.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a microscopic view of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) stained using a Ziehl-Neelsen or similar acid-fast staining technique. The bacilli appear as slender, rod-shaped organisms stained bright pink or red against a pale background. The arrangement is scattered, with no clear clustering or specific orientation. This staining method highlights the mycolic acid in the cell walls of certain bacteria, such as Mycobacterium species.

description.short_caption: CT scan of the abdomen showing gas and fluid collections in the bowel wall.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the abdomen demonstrates abnormal findings in the bowel. There are areas of gas within the bowel wall (pneumatosis intestinalis) and fluid collections, suggestive of bowel ischemia or infection. The surrounding soft tissues appear unremarkable, and no free intraperitoneal air is visible. The image is taken with contrast, as evidenced by the enhanced vascular structures.
visible_findings: gas within the bowel wall (pneumatosis intestinalis)

Case_07022/figure1.jpg.source_caption: CT of the abdomen, with annular mass.

description.short_caption: CT of the abdomen showing an annular mass in the bowel.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the abdomen demonstrates an annular mass in the bowel, indicated by arrows. The lesion appears to cause partial luminal narrowing, with thickened walls and a characteristic 'target' or 'apple-core' appearance. Surrounding structures, including adjacent bowel loops and soft tissues, appear unremarkable. No obvious signs of perforation or abscess are visible.

description.short_caption: Colonoscopy showing a yellowish plaque with surrounding inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This colonoscopy image shows a segment of the colon with a yellowish, raised plaque-like lesion surrounded by erythematous and inflamed mucosa. The lesion appears adherent to the mucosal surface, and there is evidence of surrounding tissue damage. A medical instrument is visible in the foreground, likely being used for biopsy or other intervention. The findings are suggestive of pseudomembranous colitis, often associated with Clostridioides difficile infection.

The section reveals dense inflammatory infiltrates, including numerous lymphocytes and plasma cells, within the lamina propria. There is evidence of tissue architecture disruption and possible granuloma formation. The staining highlights cellular and extracellular details, with nuclei appearing dark blue and cytoplasm in varying shades of pink.

description.short_caption: Immunohistochemical stain showing darkly stained cells amidst a background of lighter-stained tissue.

The background tissue is counterstained in a lighter blue, highlighting the cellular architecture. The distribution of the stained cells appears scattered, with no clear clustering pattern. The image is at high magnification, allowing for detailed visualization of individual cells.

Case_18002/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Triple sugar iron (TSI) agar slant of the organism after 24 hours of incubation. This slant contains glucose, sucrose, and lactose. The top portion of the slant is considered the aerobic portion due to its exposure to air and the butt of the slant is considered the anaerobic portion. Glucose fermentation is indicated by the presence of an acidic (A) reaction in the butt of the slant. Sucrose and l

description.short_caption: Triple sugar iron (TSI) agar slant showing differential fermentation results.

Case_18009/figure1.jpg.source_caption: CT chest at presentation revealed mild left upper lobe consolidation (arrow) and two lung nodules of less than 5mm in diameter.

normal lung parenchyma in other regions

Case_18008/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Fig 2: MRI of right upper extremity showing diffuse soft tissue edema and patchy enhancement involving the muscles of the right lateral chest wall, shoulder, arm, and forearm

hyperintense signal changes in subcutaneous tissues

Case_18009/figure3.jpg.source_caption: CT chest on day +11 of presentation showed a new miliary infiltrate and progressive lung consolidation (arrow).

focal consolidation in the right lung

Case_18009/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Left Lymph node biopsy. H&E stain (4x). Necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis (arrows).

description.short_caption: H&E stain (4x) showing necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis with arrows indicating necrotic areas.
description.detailed_description: This is a low-power (4x) histopathology image of a lymph node stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The tissue shows areas of necrosis (highlighted by arrows) surrounded by granulomatous inflammation. The necrotic regions appear pale and amorphous, while the surrounding granulomas are composed of dense cellular aggregates. This pattern is consistent with necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis.

Case_18009/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Direct microscopy of lymph node culture. Lactophenol cotton blue stain (40x). Numerous tuberculate, thick-walled macroconidia, between 8-15 µm in size (arrowheads) and septate hyphae (arrow).

description.short_caption: Lactophenol cotton blue stain showing tuberculate macroconidia and septate hyphae.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a lactophenol cotton blue stain of a lymph node culture at 40x magnification. Numerous thick-walled, tuberculate macroconidia, measuring approximately 8-15 µm, are visible (indicated by arrowheads). Septate hyphae are also present and highlighted by an arrow. The stain provides clear contrast, allowing detailed visualization of fungal structures.

Case_18009/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Left lung biopsy. Periodic Acid–Schiff (PAS) stain (40x). Small spherical budding yeast-forms suggestive of Histoplasma spp. observed in the cytoplasm of alveolar macrophage (arrow).

description.short_caption: PAS stain of lung biopsy showing small spherical budding yeast forms within alveolar macrophages.
description.detailed_description: This is a histopathology image of a lung biopsy stained with Periodic Acid–Schiff (PAS) at 40x magnification. The image highlights small, spherical, budding yeast forms (indicated by a red arrow) located within the cytoplasm of alveolar macrophages. The yeast forms are consistent with fungal organisms, suggestive of Histoplasma spp. The PAS stain enhances the visualization of fungal cell walls, which appear magenta against a lighter background.

Case_18011/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) showing an ill-defined mass (arrow) at the porta hepatis extending into right hepatic lobe and coursing along common bile duct with intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.

There is associated intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation, visible as dilated tubular structures within the liver parenchyma. The mass appears to obstruct the biliary flow, which is a likely cause of the ductal dilation. The arrows point to the mass and dilated ducts for clarity.
visible_findings: ill-defined mass at the porta hepatis
extension into the right hepatic lobe
coursing along the common bile duct

Case_18010/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Fig 1: CT chest with contrast at presentation demonstrating a left hilum soft tissue mass (red arrow) measured at 20 mm diameter and a left lower lobe pulmonary artery filling defect with extensive infarction and hemorrhage.

Additionally, there is a filling defect in the left lower lobe pulmonary artery, consistent with a thrombus. Surrounding the defect, there is evidence of pulmonary infarction and hemorrhage, visible as heterogeneous opacities in the left lower lobe. The contrast enhancement highlights vascular structures and the extent of the abnormalities.
visible_findings: left hilar soft tissue mass (20 mm)
left lower lobe pulmonary artery filling defect
pulmonary infarction and hemorrhage in the left lower lobe

Case_18010/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Fig 2: CT Abdomen/Pelvis with contrast showing curvilinear calcification involving most of the bladder wall (arrow).

The calcification is highlighted by the red arrow and is consistent with a pathological process affecting the bladder. Surrounding abdominal and pelvic structures appear within normal limits.
visible_findings: curvilinear calcification of the bladder wall
red arrow indicating the bladder wall

Case_18009/figure7.jpg.source_caption: Left lung biopsy. GMS stain (40x). Numerous fungal elements suggestive of histoplasmosis, in the intracellullar alveolar macrophage (arrow).

description.short_caption: GMS stain of lung biopsy showing fungal elements within alveolar macrophages.
description.detailed_description: This is a high-magnification image of lung tissue stained with Gomori methenamine silver (GMS). The stain highlights numerous small, round to oval fungal elements, which are darkly stained and located intracellularly within alveolar macrophages (indicated by the arrow). The surrounding tissue shows a network of alveolar structures with some cellular debris and background staining. The findings are consistent with fungal infection, potentially histoplasmosis.

Case_18010/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Fig 3. H&E stain of lung biopsy (200x) demonstrating a granuloma surrounding two Schistosoma spp. ova (arrows).

description.short_caption: H&E stain of lung biopsy showing granuloma with Schistosoma spp. ova.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained section of lung tissue at 200x magnification. A granuloma is visible, characterized by a central area of inflammation surrounded by epithelioid macrophages and lymphocytes. Two Schistosoma spp. ova are present within the granuloma, identifiable by their characteristic oval shape and spines (indicated by arrows). The surrounding tissue shows evidence of inflammation and cellular infiltration.
visible_findings: two Schistosoma spp. ova with characteristic spines

Case_18011/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) where multiple trematodes (arrows) were directly visualized within biliary tract (Courtesy of USC+LAC GI Endoscopy Lab)

The organisms are highlighted by arrows and are located within the bile ducts. The surrounding mucosa appears inflamed and irregular, with bile-stained areas visible. The image demonstrates direct visualization of parasitic infestation.

Case_18011/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Fasciola hepatica fluke measuring 2.6 cm in length (Courtesy of Susan Butler-Wu, PhD, D(ABBM))

description.short_caption: Fasciola hepatica fluke measuring approximately 2.6 cm in length.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a preserved Fasciola hepatica fluke placed on a clear surface next to a ruler for scale. The fluke is leaf-shaped, with a flattened body and visible internal structures, including branching dark lines suggestive of its digestive or reproductive system. The ruler indicates the fluke's length is approximately 2.6 cm. The specimen is labeled as part of a pathology collection.

Case_18012/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2: CT scan of the neck. A soft tissue density is seen in the subcutaneous tissue on the right side of the neck with skin thickening and adjacent fat stranding without evidence of a fluid collection.

description.short_caption: Axial CT of the neck showing subcutaneous soft tissue density with fat stranding on the right.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the neck demonstrates a soft tissue density in the subcutaneous tissue on the right side, marked by a red circle. visible_findings: soft tissue density in subcutaneous tissue

Case_18012/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Figure 1: Neck lesion at presentation (A) and after removal of the eschar (B)

description.short_caption: Neck lesion before (A) and after eschar removal (B).

Panel A depicts an erythematous, indurated lesion with a central dark eschar surrounded by scaling and inflammation. Panel B shows the same lesion after removal of the eschar, revealing an ulcerated base with surrounding erythema and scaling. The lesion is located on the posterior neck near the hairline.
visible_findings: ulcerated base after eschar removal in panel B

Case_18012/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Figure 3b: Several intracytoplasmic bodies (arrow) are seen measuring around 2 micrometer (400x magnification). These are consistent with amastigotes. Each amastigote has a prominent kinetoplast.

The amastigotes are small, measuring approximately 2 micrometers, and each contains a prominent kinetoplast, which is a distinguishing feature. The surrounding tissue includes inflammatory cells and appears to be part of a granulomatous response. The image is magnified at 400x.

Case_18011/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Single trematode (arrow) within biliary tract at ERCP. (Courtesy of LAC +USC GI Endoscopy Lab)

visible_findings: single trematode with branching internal structures
bile and debris in the lumen

Case_18012/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Figure 3A: Dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate is seen with pan-dermal granulomas (40x magnification).

Case_18011/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Fasciola hepatica egg measuring 130µM x 75µM obtained from stool sample. (Courtesy of Susan Butler-Wu, PhD, D(ABBM))

Case_18012/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Figure 4: Serial photography of the neck lesion

Case_18013/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Figure 1: Photograph of right foot showing 12cm x 7cm swelling with exophytic nodules

Case_18018/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2: Double disk synergy test and combined-disk test with Imipenem alone (A) and with EDTA disk tests (B). The picture shows a combined disk test that uses the disk of imipenem alone (IMP) and the disk of imipenem plus EDTA (IMP-EDTA). An enhanced inhibition zone of more than 7 mm around IMP + EDTA is seen when a metallo-beta-lactamase is present.

description.short_caption: Double disk synergy test showing enhanced inhibition with IMP + EDTA disk.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a culture plate with two disks labeled 'IMP' (imipenem alone) and 'IMP + EDTA' (imipenem plus EDTA). The plate demonstrates a clear enhancement of the inhibition zone around the IMP + EDTA disk compared to the IMP disk alone. This finding is consistent with the presence of a metallo-beta-lactamase enzyme, which is inhibited by EDTA. The test is a combined disk test used to detect metallo-beta-lactamase production in bacterial isolates.
visible_findings: enhanced inhibition zone around 'IMP + EDTA' disk

The findings are suggestive of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL) with associated parasitic infection.
